blocking.section: Decision outcome > Confirmation (FIPS job, line 100) and Consequences (line 90)
blocking.issue: The FIPS test lets a FIPS Node treat `http3: true` as 'inert'. Foundation pack section 8.1 rules that out, and ADR-0001 rejects it explicitly. ADR-0001 also leaves FIPS handling of `http3: true` open under OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9, so this ADR pre-empts that question and contradicts ADR-0001 on it. The ADR also never says that turning HTTP/3 off makes the FIPS build differ in features. Foundation pack section 1 ('with the same features') and P1 ('one feature set in every public build, including the FIPS build') forbid that difference; only pack section 8.4 allows it, and only while OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9 is open. Line 90 cites section 8.4 but not the P1 exception it creates.
blocking.evidence: Line 100: "- **FIPS job**, Planned (M5): fails if quic-go appears in the FIPS `ruralzd` dependencies ([ADR-0001](0001-implementation-language-go.md)), and FIPS tests assert that `http3: true` is refused or inert." Foundation pack 8.1: "Equal digests mean equal effective behavior on every Node that accepts them". ADR-0001 line 51: "How a FIPS Node treats a Revision with `http3: true` is open: ignoring the field would break equal behavior for equal digests (foundation pack section 8.1) ... The owning document MUST add this case to OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9." Vision P1: "one feature set in every public build, including the FIPS build." Foundation pack section 1: "A build flavor (`GOFIPS140`, Planned (M5)) with the same features and license as the default build".
blocking.fix: Replace the clause after the ADR-0001 link on line 100 with: "and FIPS tests assert that a FIPS `ruralzd` never binds UDP 8443 and never silently ignores `http3: true` (foundation pack section 8.1); how it rejects the field follows OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9." Fold the end of line 90 ("that G3 exception is why HTTP/3 is off in FIPS builds (foundation pack section 8.4)") into a new Consequences bullet: "Bad, because FIPS builds lack HTTP/3, a feature difference that foundation pack section 1 and P1 otherwise forbid, allowed only by pack section 8.4 until OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9 closes ([ADR-0001](0001-implementation-language-go.md))." The body is at 1,494 of 1,500 words, so offset the new words by shortening the v0.62.0 priorities bullet on line 109 or the 'Other servers' row.

blocking.issue: The 'because' clause misstates foundation pack section 7. Most protocol libraries in that section are clients or brokers with no `net/http` handler: franz-go, nats.go/jetstream, paho.golang, mochi-mqtt, the grpc-go upstream client and rueidis. Only connect-go in section 7 composes with `net/http` handlers. coder/websocket and SSE flushing compose with them too, but they appear in the Tech stack catalog, not in section 7. The decision's stated rationale therefore contradicts the binding pack it cites.
blocking.evidence: Line 42: "Chosen option: \"`net/http` for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and h2c, plus quic-go for HTTP/3\", because every protocol library in foundation pack section 7 composes with `net/http` handlers,". Foundation pack section 7: "| Messaging | `twmb/franz-go` (Kafka), `nats.go/jetstream`, `eclipse-paho/paho.golang` (MQTT 5 client) + `mochi-mqtt` embedded broker mode `Planned (M4)` | ADR-0013 |" and "| gRPC ingress / upstream | `connectrpc.com/connect` (gRPC, gRPC-Web, Connect on `net/http`); `grpc-go` for upstream clients |".
blocking.fix: Replace the clause with: "because the ingress libraries, connect-go (foundation pack section 7), coder/websocket and `http.ResponseController` SSE flushing ([Library catalog](../engineering/01-tech-stack-and-libraries.md#library-catalog)), compose with `net/http` handlers,". This adds about ten words, so trim the same number elsewhere (see L2-1). It closes L1-4 as well.

blocking.issue: The driver says S3 is a requirement, but the depends_on Tech stack document makes only G1 to G3 mandatory. S3 is a soft criterion that libraries SHOULD meet, checked by design review. As written, the driver raises a SHOULD to a MUST, which that document contradicts.
blocking.evidence: Line 26: "- **Composition with selected libraries**: criterion S3 requires `net/http` handlers and `context.Context` cancellation ([Selection criteria](../engineering/01-tech-stack-and-libraries.md#selection-criteria))." Tech stack, Selection criteria: "Every dependency MUST pass gates G1 to G3 and SHOULD score well on the rest." and "| S3 | Composes with `net/http` handlers and `context.Context` cancellation | Design review |".
blocking.fix: Change the wording without adding words: "soft criterion S3 favors `net/http` handlers and `context.Context` cancellation". If the hard constraint matters, cite it separately: connect-go serves only on `net/http` handlers, which line 36 already sources.

blocking.section: Decision drivers (line 27) and Decision outcome (HTTP/3 row, line 49)
blocking.issue: The ADR names bounded resources as a driver 'as the data plane's Bounded resources table fixes them'. Every mechanism in that table is TCP- or HTTP2Config-specific, though, and the HTTP/3 row sets no ceiling for quic-go connections, streams, flow-control windows or header size. The result contradicts System overview's 'Bounded everything' design rule, which component decisions MUST NOT break without saying so. Nothing in the foundation documents or the research gives quic-go limits, so the ADR has to route the gap to the owning document instead of implying it is covered. This is the same gap as L1-1, and one fix closes both.
blocking.evidence: Line 27: "- **Bounded resources**: per-connection stream, buffer and frame limits and per-request deadlines, as the data plane's [Bounded resources](../architecture/03-data-plane.md#bounded-resources) table fixes them." Line 49: "| HTTP/3 | quic-go `http3` v0.63.x, pinned, on UDP at the `https` listener's port when `http3: true`, with the same Routes, Policies and certificates, behind an internal interface; a build constraint keeps it out of FIPS builds (OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9) | Planned (M3) |". System overview, Design principles: "| Bounded everything | Every queue, buffer, pool, retry, fan-out, retired snapshot and per-key bucket table (LRU) has a ceiling. |". Data plane: "| Client connections per Node | 20,000 connections (target); a counting `net.Listener` stops calling `Accept` at the ceiling |".
blocking.fix: Add to the HTTP/3 row: "QUIC connections and streams count against the Node connection and in-flight ceilings, and quic-go stream, flow-control and header limits stay at or below the HTTP/2 values (target); the quic-go settings await research". Add to the 'Proposed owning-document amendments' bullet: "Data plane SHOULD add HTTP/3 rows to Bounded resources and an Open question naming the quic-go limits and `http.ResponseController` deadline support." Offset the words as in L2-1.

non_blocking.suggestion: The dashed path quic-go -> handler -> connect-go and coder/websocket suggests that native gRPC and WebSocket work over HTTP/3. Multi-protocol says "native gRPC and WebSocket need TCP" (line 76) and "Extended CONNECT over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 is Not planned" (line 285). Add "native gRPC and WebSocket stay on TCP" to the caption.

non_blocking.section: Considered options, Decision outcome, Pros and cons
non_blocking.suggestion: The chosen option has three names: Considered option 1 ("`net/http` for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and h2c through `Server.Protocols` and `HTTP2Config`, plus quic-go `http3` for HTTP/3"), the Chosen option string ("`net/http` for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and h2c, plus quic-go for HTTP/3") and the H3 "net/http plus quic-go". MADR traceability is better when the Chosen option string and the H3 reuse one short name, with the same name in bold at the start of each Considered options item.

"Ruralz Control serves the REST API and Ruralz Console on 8090 and the Control Stream on 8091 through `connectrpc.com/connect` in gRPC mode" can be read as saying the REST API uses connect in gRPC mode. Reorder it: "serves the Control Stream on 8091 through `connectrpc.com/connect` in gRPC mode, and the REST API and Ruralz Console on 8090".

"the Planned (M4) benchmark suite reports them separately" does not match Performance budgets PB-8 ("Ruralz-owned allocations per S1 request, `net/http` internals excluded | 30 or fewer (target) | `testing.AllocsPerRun` ... | Planned (M1)") or the Testing strategy alloc/op gate, which is Planned (M1). Write "the Planned (M1) PB-8 allocation gate excludes them", and keep the M4 suite only for the published comparison. PB-8 tags the figure (target) while System overview tags it (hypothesis); the ADR follows System overview, which is acceptable, but the mismatch is worth a note to the performance document.

The catalog-row ban lives in Repository layout and conventions, Banned imports ("Any module without a catalog row | Add a row in the same pull request"), so link that table as well. A depguard deny for `github.com/valyala/fasthttp` would make the rejection machine-checked instead of relying on review. Add it to the proposed Repository layout amendment in More information.

"low-level types such as `Framer` stay supported" uses 'supported', the word the style guide bans as an availability tag. It refers to an upstream API, not a Ruralz feature, so it is allowed, but "are not deprecated" matches the research wording (tooling-and-licenses section 5: "Not deprecated") and cannot be misread.

`docs/_meta/research/go-libraries-protocols.md` has no net/http, HTTP/2 or quic-go section. The ADR correctly draws its HTTP facts from `docs/_meta/research/go-libraries-runtime.md` section 3 and `tooling-and-licenses.md` section 5. The manifest entry should list go-libraries-runtime.md, so reviewers check the right source.

The verifier counts 1,494 body words against the adr_common maximum of 1,500. The L1 and L2 fixes add about 80 words, so they need offsets. Candidates: drop the v0.62.0 priorities bullet (line 109), merge the 'Update review' Confirmation item into the dependency admission item, and shorten the 'Other servers' row. Do not delete text that closes these findings.

`docs/adr/0015-zero-downtime-upgrades-so-reuseport.md` does not exist yet, so the verifier warns about lines 92 and 136. The path matches the manifest, so no change is needed, but check again once ADR-0015 lands.

foundation_amendments: Foundation pack section 1 (FIPS build row) says the FIPS flavor has 'the same features and license as the default build', but section 8.4 turns HTTP/3 off in FIPS builds (OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-9), and vision P1 says 'one feature set in every public build, including the FIPS build'.
